ordered_diagnoses: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with divergent differentiation

facts.raw_span: A 50-year-old man
known neurofibromatosis type 1
multiple cutaneous neurofibromas
no history of smoking
recurrent urinary retention and sepsis
transurethral resection of the prostate revealed fibroleiomyomatous hyperplasia
diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall without a discrete mass
bladder wall was diffusely thickened, firm, and gray–white, with near–complete loss of the detrusor muscle
diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix
dense, perivascular spindle cell proliferation with prominent cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern
tumor cells were positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56
tumor cells were negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin

concepts.why: The patient has a history of neurofibromatosis type 1 and the tumor cells show a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix, which is consistent with MPNST.
The patient has a history of neurofibromatosis type 1 and multiple cutaneous neurofibromas, which suggests a possible diagnosis of neurofibroma.
The tumor cells are positive for S100, which is a marker for schwannomas, and the patient has a history of neurofibromatosis type 1.
The patient presents with recurrent urinary retention and sepsis, which could be symptoms of a urinary tract infection.
The patient has diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall without a discrete mass, which could be consistent with interstitial cystitis.
The patient has a diffusely thickened bladder wall with near-complete loss of the detrusor muscle, which could be consistent with a bladder sarcoma.
The patient has diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall without a discrete mass, which could be consistent with urothelial carcinoma.
The patient has a transurethral resection of the prostate that revealed fibroleiomyomatous hyperplasia.

concepts.preferred_label: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with divergent differentiation
concepts.why: The tumor cells were negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin, which is consistent with the immunohistochemical profile of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors with divergent differentiation.

rationales.F02: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is strongly associated with malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
rationales.F10: The presence of cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern is indicative of a malignant tumor.
rationales.F11: The tumor cells' positivity for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56 is consistent with a diagnosis of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
rationales.F12: The tumor cells' negativity for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin helps to rule out other tumor types.
